dossier.description: Root namespace. Every key is resolved through the settings cascade (.claude/settings.dossier.local.json > .claude/settings.dossier.json > $HOME/.claude/settings.dossier.json > plugin settings.json), with DOSSIER_* environment variables overriding all four. The env layer is what lets a CI job run with zero interaction. One deliberate exception: bin/dossier-validate-patch.sh reads the file cascade only and ignores the env layer, because it runs in the same environment as the agent it contains and the value it reads is the write allowlist — an agent able to set DOSSIER_CI_WRITE_ALLOWLIST could widen its own boundary. The project-local cascade layer is likewise honoured only while it is untracked.

project.description: Project identity and where the package is written. Corresponds to PROJECT_NAME / PROJECT_MISSION / PROJECT_ROOT_OR_SOURCES / DOCUMENTATION_OUTPUT_ROOT / PROJECT_VERSION_OR_COMMIT in the invocation contract.

name.description: Canonical project name used in every document header and in the terminology register. Empty means unresolved; /dossier:init asks for it rather than inferring, because an inferred product name silently propagates into public documents.

mission.description: One-paragraph statement of problem, users, and intended outcome. Empty is legitimate — the package records it as Unknown and derives what it can from evidence rather than inventing intent.

items.description: A repository-relative or sibling path the run may inspect.

sources.description: Roots the run may inspect. Multiple entries support multi-repo projects. Anything outside this list is out of scope and is reported as an inspection-coverage gap rather than silently skipped.

outputRoot.description: Where the 23-file package is written. Relative-only by pattern so that engagement.allowedActions.writeOutsideOutputRoot is mechanically checkable — an absolute path would make the containment check meaningless.

versionOrCommit.description: The version the package describes. 'auto' resolves to the current commit SHA at run start and pins it for the whole run, so a package never mixes evidence from two revisions.

type.description: Project classification. Drives section-level adaptation only — never the file set. 'auto' classifies from evidence in Phase 1 and records the classification with its supporting evidence IDs.

engagement.description: Why the package is being produced and what the run is permitted to do.

deliveryMode.description: full = inspect the whole scope and build/rebuild the package. targeted = identify changed evidence, update affected and downstream documents, then check the whole package for contradictions. verification-only = audit and write the verification report, repairing nothing unless allowedActions permits it.

dueDiligenceContext.description: The decision being supported, its decision maker, stage, materiality thresholds, risk appetite, and horizon. Empty produces a general technical and product readiness assessment — never invented transaction-specific acceptance criteria.

audience.description: Which documentation audience they belong to.

stakeholders.description: Known stakeholders. Feeds the ownership register and the pass-C audience personas. Never used to invent an owner: components with no evidenced owner are recorded 'unassigned'.

constraints.description: Access, environment, confidentiality, platform, or cost constraints. Each one that blocks a check becomes a 'not executed' entry with this as its reason, rather than an unexplained gap.

items.description: One candidate regime. Listing it does not establish applicability.

regulatory.description: Applicable jurisdictions, industries, contracts, or policies. Listing one here does not make it applicable — applicability itself is a claim requiring evidence.

allowedActions.description: The action ceiling. Resolved in Phase 0 and immutable for the run; a run that widens its own ceiling mid-flight produces a package nobody can audit. Defaults are restrictive because the safe failure is an under-verified claim honestly labelled, not an unauthorized action.

readSource.description: Read project source, config, and history.

readSecrets.description: Off by default and rarely worth enabling: a secret's value is never needed to document that it exists, only its type, location category, and rotation story.

runBuild.description: Execute documented build commands to verify they work. Off by default because builds run arbitrary project code.

runTests.description: Execute documented test commands. Off by default for the same reason as runBuild. When off, every setup/build/test claim is marked 'not executed' rather than assumed to pass.

networkAccess.description: Reach external sources to verify vendor lifecycle status, CVEs, or license terms. Off by default; when off, such claims are labelled rather than answered from model memory.

writeOutsideOutputRoot.description: Write anywhere other than project.outputRoot. Off by default and enforced by a PreToolUse hook, not merely by instruction.

contactHumans.description: Ask blocking questions of a human. Off by default in CI; non-blocking unknowns always go to the open-questions register instead of stalling the package.

disclosure.description: Governs everything under 06-public/. A public document is an unretractable commitment, so the defaults here are the most conservative in the file.

policy.description: Default classification for material not otherwise classified. 'internal-only' is the default because when the disclosure boundary is unknown the correct behaviour is to draft public documents without releasing them, not to guess what is safe to say.

publicClaimApproval.description: Whether a public claim needs recorded human approval before it can be marked approved. Default 'required': the run may apply a policy but may never appoint itself the business, legal, security, or communications approver. Unapproved claims stay 'pending' and block the release gate.

confidentialityDefault.description: Confidentiality stamped on an internal document header when its content does not dictate otherwise.

items.description: An extended regular expression scanned for in public content.

redactionPatterns.description: Extra regexes scanned for in 06-public/ content, on top of the built-in credential patterns. Project-specific additions such as customer names or internal hostnames belong here.

package.description: Structural contract for the generated package.

requireAll23.description: Require every canonical file to exist. True by default and rarely worth changing: a package whose shape varies per project cannot be diffed, audited, or compared across engagements. Irrelevant topics are handled with a justified N/A at section level, not by dropping the file.

allowExtraFiles.description: Permit supplemental documents alongside the canonical set. They must be linked from the documentation index and must not duplicate a canonical source of truth.

headerStyle.description: Header contract version. Enumerated with one value so that a future header change is a versioned migration rather than a silent reformat.

verification.description: The three-pass independent audit. Independence is architectural: separate agent dispatches, memory: none, and a skill firewall that keeps reconciliation logic out of every verifier's context.

passes.description: Which passes to run. A = evidence and coverage, B = model falsification, C = audience, consistency, and disclosure. Narrowing this is a deliberate reduction in assurance and is recorded in the verification report.

passModels.description: Per-pass model override. A plugin cannot guarantee a genuinely different model, so this is the honest half-measure: independent context always, different model when you configure it. Use /dossier:audit --external for true cross-model independence.

A.description: Model for pass A. 'inherit' means OMIT the dispatch override so the agent's `model: inherit` frontmatter selects the session model — it is not itself a value the Agent tool accepts. The other four are the only valid override values; a full model ID such as 'claude-opus-5' is rejected at dispatch, which is why this is an enum rather than a free string.

B.description: Model for pass B. 'inherit' means OMIT the dispatch override so the agent's `model: inherit` frontmatter selects the session model — it is not itself a value the Agent tool accepts. The other four are the only valid override values; a full model ID such as 'claude-opus-5' is rejected at dispatch, which is why this is an enum rather than a free string.

C.description: Model for pass C. 'inherit' means OMIT the dispatch override so the agent's `model: inherit` frontmatter selects the session model — it is not itself a value the Agent tool accepts. The other four are the only valid override values; a full model ID such as 'claude-opus-5' is rejected at dispatch, which is why this is an enum rather than a free string.

claimSample.description: How much of the ledger each pass audits.

minRows.description: Floor on sampled rows, so a small package is not audited by a sample of three.

percent.description: Percentage of lower-impact internal claims sampled. The sampling method and size are stated in the verification report — an unstated sample is not evidence.

items.description: A claim category audited at 100 percent, never sampled.

auditAllCategories.description: Categories audited at 100%, never sampled. These are the claims where a single wrong row changes a transaction, security, or legal decision.

traceCount.description: End-to-end traces pass B executes against the sources. Minimum 3 because the model must be tested against at least one primary flow, one change-to-production flow, and one failure or abuse flow.

maxRounds.description: Audit/repair rounds before the run stops and reports conditionally-ready with exact blockers. Bounded so a package that cannot converge produces an honest verdict rather than an infinite loop.

gate.description: The release gate. Binary and conjunctive — a score is not a gate.

minScore.description: Total scorecard minimum. 95 matches the source contract; lowering it is a local policy decision that the verification report records verbatim.

minDimensionPercent.description: Each dimension must reach this percentage of its available points. Prevents a package averaging well while failing one dimension outright.

requireAllConditions.description: Require all 16 gate conditions. True by default: a package can score 96 and still be unreleasable on one unsupported public claim.

failOn.description: Unresolved finding severities that block release.

stalenessDays.description: Age at which a document's last-verified date makes its claims stale, independent of whether code changed. Surfaces in /dossier:status and is one of the documented refresh triggers.

maxStaleDocsPerSweep.description: Ceiling on how many stale documents a single schedule-triggered sweep hands to dossier-policy.sh for re-verification, most-overdue first. Bounds a scheduled run's cost when many documents have gone stale simultaneously; it does not bound how many can be reported as stale by /dossier:status.

ci.description: The post-merge documentation job. Only the parts GitHub must evaluate before a runner exists live in the workflow YAML; everything here is read at runtime by dossier-policy.sh, so policy changes need no workflow edit.

enabled.description: Master switch. False makes the policy job exit with reason=disabled after ~40 seconds and zero tokens.

triggerPolicy.description: Default is path-filtered merge composed with a scheduled sweep. They compose safely because refresh is range-based against a durable cursor: a wrong path filter costs latency, never correctness. label-gated is available but not the default — its failure mode is quietly stale documentation that looks current, which is the exact failure this plugin exists to prevent.

branchStrategy.description: rolling = one long-lived branch, one accumulating PR. Chosen as default because a 23-file package regenerated from overlapping ranges produces mutually-conflicting edits to the same files on every per-PR branch; per-pr multiplies merge cost by N while appearing to isolate. Per-run traceability is preserved by commit trailers.

rollingBranch.description: Branch name. Its prefix is also the strongest loop guard, so changing it requires re-running /dossier:setup to re-render the workflow's if: expression.

rollingBranchRotation.description: Rotate the rolling branch so the open PR never becomes a 400-commit monster nobody reviews. Recommended for high-volume repos.

instructionSource.description: plugin = CI installs from the marketplace via plugin_marketplaces, which accepts no ref — so the skill text always tracks marketplace main even when bin/ scripts are pinned. vendored = copy the refresh instructions into the repo for full pinning. Choose vendored when you need reproducible CI or the marketplace is private.

forkPolicy.description: warn = notice and let the scheduled sweep cover fork PRs (GitHub withholds secrets from fork pull_request runs by design). target = use pull_request_target, safe here only because we never check out PR head. skip = silent.

generated.description: Applied to every generated documentation pull request. Also a loop guard: a PR carrying it never triggers a refresh.

force.description: Applied by a human to force a refresh for a pull request the trigger policy would otherwise skip.

skip.description: Applied by a human to suppress the refresh for one pull request.

oversized.description: Applied when the generated diff exceeds the document thresholds, so an unusually large docs PR is visibly flagged rather than quietly merged.

labels.description: Label names. 'generated' and the branch prefix are independent loop guards; keep both.

items.description: A glob whose change should trigger a documentation refresh.

include.description: Rendered into the workflow's on.pull_request.paths, so a non-matching merge costs literally zero.

items.description: A glob whose change should not trigger a refresh.

exclude.description: Applied at runtime after the coarse filter. Must contain the outputRoot glob, which is what makes a merged docs PR fail the policy check even if every other loop guard were removed.

apiSurfaceGlobs.description: Paths whose diff is extracted separately into the evidence bundle, because an interface change has outsized documentation impact relative to its line count.

minChangedFiles.description: Minimum changed files before a refresh is worth running. Default 1: any real change is worth documenting, and the path filters already removed the noise.

maxSourceDiffLines.description: Refuse ranges above this. Catches vendored-dependency drops that would burn a run's whole budget on noise.

maxSourceDiffBytes.description: Cap on source.diff in the evidence bundle. Beyond it the diff is truncated and flagged, and the agent reads files from the checkout instead — strictly better evidence, and it keeps a $0.50 run from becoming a $15 one.

maxDocChangedFiles.description: Document count above which the generated diff is treated as oversized. Default 30 sits above a normal targeted refresh and below a full regeneration.

maxDocChangedLines.description: Line count above which the generated diff is treated as oversized.

oversizedBehavior.description: What to do when the generated diff exceeds the doc thresholds. 'draft' opens the PR as a draft and labels it, because an oversized diff is usually the correct output of a cold start or a major refactor and discarding it destroys real work.

maxDocPrsPer24h.description: Refuse to start further runs above this rate. Catches refresh loops. Note this bounds loop count, not cost per run — GitHub Actions has no spend cap for third-party API calls.

model.description: Model for the CI refresh, passed through to the action's --model. Empty inherits the action default and emits no flag at all. Pattern-constrained to a single bare token: the value is interpolated into the workflow's claude_args block, so whitespace would split into stray arguments. This is the CLI surface, so a full model ID is valid here — unlike verification.passModels, which is the Agent-tool surface.

maxTurns.description: Hard turn ceiling passed as --max-turns. Bounds a single run's cost.

enabled.description: The sweep that catches whatever the path filters missed. Cheap: on a current repo the policy job exits in ~40s having spent zero tokens.

cron.description: Sweep schedule. Weekly on Monday morning by default: often enough that a missed merge is documented within days, rare enough to stay nearly free.

minCommits.description: Minimum commits in the range before the scheduled sweep does any work. Default 1, so a quiet week costs one short policy job and no tokens.

items.description: A glob a CI run may modify. Anything else aborts the run.

writeAllowlist.description: The only paths a CI run may modify. Enforced twice — once in the unprivileged refresh job and again, independently, in the privileged publish job. The second check is the control; the first is a convenience. An escape is a hard failure, never a silent filter, because a silent filter hides the attempt.

expectedPluginVersion.description: Plugin version the rendered workflow was generated against. A mismatch tells you to re-run /dossier:setup.

onFlowMerge.description: Behaviour when the flow plugin completes a merge locally. 'suggest' is the default because the local path is cheaper and simpler than CI but has weaker coverage — it only fires for merges that go through /flow:merge, missing web-UI and merge-queue merges.

tiers.description: Safety tier per action class. Promotion (autonomous -> journal -> confirm) is always allowed; demotion is a deliberate reduction in safety and is recorded.
